title: Should baseURI for initial top level javascript URIs be the creators base?
body: ### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? See [wpt test](https://wpt.fyi/results/html/infrastructure/urls/base-url/initial-about-blank-baseURI.window.html?label=master&product=chrome%5Bexperimental%5D&product=edge%5Bexperimental%5D&product=firefox%5Bexperimental%5D&product=safari%5Bexperimental%5D&product=servo&aligned&q=base-url%2Finitial-about-blank-baseURI) and Firefox [bug 2020147](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2020147) `window.open('/').document.baseURI` and `window.open('javascript:0;').document.baseURI` are `about:blank` in Blink and WebKit, while it is the creator's base URI in Gecko. In the case of iframes, the wpt shows that all engines use the embedder's base URI for initial temporary / transient `about:blank`. According to [#creating-a-new-browsing-context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#creating-a-new-browsing-context), the about base URL of a new document starts out as the creator's document base URL. I believe the specified behavior makes sense, is more consistent and that Firefox is correct. But the only example I can come up with where this might matter is something like `window.open(javascript:'')` not working in Blink / WebKit. Thus I believe the difference isn't of significance to web pages and it would be easy to align Firefox to Blink / WebKit. Though updating the spec to reflect that behavior seems less trivial to me. Would Blink / WebKit be open to adjust their implementation? cc @zcorpan
